name: Paracas culture
title: The story of the Paracas culture

text: About 2,800 years ago, the Paracas people lived on the dry south coast of Peru.
They lived in groups led by chiefs, joined by shared beliefs and trade, but not always at peace.
src: The Paracas culture flourished on the south coast of Peru from about 800 to 100 BCE / The dry coast preserved them
It was made up of local chiefdoms, joined by shared religion and trade / relations between them were not always peaceful

text: Their weavers made some of the finest cloth of the ancient Andes, from cotton and llama and alpaca hair.
They wrapped their dead, sitting up, in many layers of fine cloth.
src: the Paracas Necropolis textiles are considered among the finest ever produced in the Pre-Columbian Andes / Weavers used native cotton and the hair of the vicuña, llama and alpaca
Its dead were bound in a seated position and wrapped in many layers of finely woven and embroidered cloth

text: The Paracas people made the oldest known skull operations in the Americas, scraping and drilling away parts of the skull.
Nearly 40 out of every 100 patients lived on for a long time afterwards.
src: The Paracas culture also shows the earliest trepanations in the Americas, made by scraping and drilling away parts of the skull

text: They made pictures on the land, on hillsides, a thousand years before the Nazca Lines.
Scholars believe the Paracas culture later grew into the Nazca culture, which kept its beliefs and its weaving.
src: Many of the geoglyphs of Palpa province stand on hillsides / shown to predate the Nazca Lines by a thousand years
The Paracas culture is believed to have evolved into the Nazca culture, which shared its religion and carried on its textile making
